tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (why is the app slow, where is the bottleneck, will it scale), explicitly lists trigger contexts and symptom keywords (latency, p99, timeouts, throttling, queue backlog), and covers the service scope concisely while remaining focused on outcomes rather than internal mechanics.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks why an application or service is slow, where the latency comes from, what the bottleneck is, whether resources are right-sized, or whether the workload will scale for a peak. ... Triggers on "performance review", "why is it slow", "bottleneck", "backlog", "p99".

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific procedures (RED/USE methods, Well-Architected mapping, specific AWS APIs) without explaining general concepts the agent already knows. Every sentence carries domain-specific signal.
tests.evidence: Native AWS read APIs only: CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs, X-Ray, Application Signals, Compute Optimizer, Trusted Advisor, Database Insights (`pi` API) and the describe APIs of the services on the path.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/consistency-critical operations (magnitude checks, hygiene rules, API call bounding) are given exact prescriptive rules, while open-ended diagnostic reasoning (Step 4 differential, Step 2 path mapping) explains the why and leaves room for judgment appropriate to investigative work.
tests.evidence: A Confirmed cause must account for the measured symptom in numbers... Keep API calls bounded: one `GetMetricData` call per resource with all its metrics.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic methodology (RED/USE, differential diagnosis, right-sizing) applicable to any AWS performance investigation, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Traces the path from the entry point (load balancer, queue, stream or schedule) through its dependencies, finds the constraining resource with the USE and RED methods, and returns ranked fixes mapped to Well-Architected best practices.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Top gotchas' section with 14 concrete, non-obvious domain-specific corrections (e.g., Lambda memory sets CPU, cold start rules, retry amplification proof).
tests.evidence: 4. **Lambda memory is the CPU setting.** Read Lambda `MemorySize` (with the `REPORT` line as fallback) before judging CPU; low memory use is not headroom on a CPU-bound function.
